candidates.authorityName: California Department of Fish and Wildlife

parameters.note: Duncan Creek is a named right-bank (north-side) tributary of the Middle Fork American River, joining it at 3,379 ft elevation below French Meadows Reservoir, and is one of the primary named streams of the Middle Fork American River Project (Placer County Water Agency, FERC No. 2079). It is not listed by name in CCR §7.40(b) or §7.50(b), so it falls under the general statewide stream regulation §5.85(a)(2): open with a five-trout bag from the last Saturday in April through November 15, then a zero-trout catch-and-release period with gear restrictions from November 16 through the Friday preceding the last Saturday in April.

end.verbatim: the Friday preceding the last Saturday in April

candidates.summary: Open the last Saturday in April through November 15 (general statewide stream regulation; not listed as a special-regulation water); November 16 through the Friday preceding the last Saturday in April is a zero-trout, artificial-lures-with-barbless-hooks period

candidates.authorityName: California Department of Fish and Wildlife

parameters.counting_rule: General statewide trout limit for inland streams, rivers, and canals: five-trout daily bag limit and ten-trout possession limit, in effect from the last Saturday in April through November 15.

candidates.summary: 5 trout daily bag limit, 10 trout possession limit, last Saturday in April through November 15

candidates.authorityName: California Department of Fish and Wildlife

parameters.counting_rule: Zero-trout bag limit from November 16 through the Friday preceding the last Saturday in April; trout must be released unharmed and should not be removed from the water.

candidates.summary: Zero-trout bag limit (catch-and-release for trout), November 16 through the Friday preceding the last Saturday in April

parameters.note: Gear restriction applies from November 16 through the Friday preceding the last Saturday in April, for all species of fish. During the regular season (last Saturday in April through November 15) the general stream regulation imposes no gear restrictions.

candidates.citation: CEQAnet — Duncan Creek Diversion Improvement Project; Granite Construction — Duncan Creek Diversion Dam Improvement Project

parameters.description: Duncan Creek carries a Placer County Water Agency (PCWA) diversion dam (the Duncan Creek Diversion Dam, part of the Middle Fork American River Project, FERC No. 2079) located on Tahoe National Forest land about 1.5 miles above the creek's confluence area, roughly 1.5 miles north of French Meadows Reservoir. PCWA completed dam improvements including a new fish-screening facility to prevent entrainment and provide downstream fish passage, and new gates/piping to manage instream flows below the diversion.

raw.improvements: fish screening facility (entrainment prevention, downstream fish passage); new gates and piping for instream-flow management

candidates.summary: Duncan Creek is regulated by a PCWA diversion dam (Middle Fork American River Project, FERC No. 2079) on Tahoe National Forest land upstream of the creek's lower reach; the dam was upgraded with a fish-screening facility for downstream fish passage and new instream-flow controls.
